people.name: Stephanie VandenBerg
people.bio: Stephanie VandenBerg is the Republican nominee for Jefferson County Commissioner, District 3. She is a certified public accountant who owns a small business in Jefferson County, and she previously served as treasurer of a Jeffco charter school. Her campaign says her family has lived in Jefferson County since 2014 and in Deer Creek Canyon since 2018.

people.name: Lisa A. Cutter
people.bio: Lisa Cutter, a Democrat, is a Colorado state senator representing Senate District 20 (since January 2023) and previously served in the Colorado House, District 25, from 2019 to 2023. Her campaign says she runs a communications firm and lives in Jefferson County.

people.name: Paul Poston
people.bio: Paul Poston is the Republican nominee for Jefferson County Clerk and Recorder.

people.name: Nicole Hensel
people.bio: Nicole Hensel is the Democratic nominee for Jefferson County Clerk and Recorder. Her campaign describes her as a former teacher, organizer and nonprofit leader who has worked on election-protection and voting-policy efforts.

people.name: Eric Proctor
people.bio: Eric Proctor is the Democratic nominee for Jefferson County Treasurer. He describes himself as a community banker and a former public school teacher, and he has held Democratic Party posts including Jefferson County Democratic Party secretary.

people.name: Murl Hendrickson
people.bio: Murl Hendrickson is the Libertarian Party candidate for Jefferson County Treasurer. His campaign says he lives in Arvada, works as an associate financial representative, holds a B.A. in economics from the University of Colorado, and is completing Certified Financial Planner certification.

endorsements.title: Former Weld RE-8 School Board Member

people.name: Vera King
people.bio: Vera King is the Republican nominee for Jefferson County Assessor. The Critical Report describes her as a community advocate.

people.name: Andy Kerr
people.bio: Andy Kerr, a Democrat, is the Jefferson County Commissioner for District 2, a seat he has held since 2021. He served in the Colorado House (District 26) from 2006 to 2013 and the Colorado Senate (District 22) from 2013 to 2019, and he previously taught in Jeffco Public Schools.

people.name: Greg Ketcham
people.bio: Greg Ketcham is an unaffiliated candidate for Jefferson County Assessor. His campaign says he is a certified general appraiser who has worked as a residential and commercial appraiser in the Jefferson County Assessor's Office since 2017, and that he was born and raised in Littleton.

people.name: Regina "Reggie" Marinelli
people.bio: Reggie Marinelli, a Democrat, has been Jefferson County Sheriff since January 2023 and is seeking re-election. According to the Sheriff's Office, she has worked there for more than 36 years, with supervisory roles in patrol, detentions, investigations and support services, and she commanded the West Metro Drug Task Force from 2012 to 2015.

finance.report: August 4, 2026 - Report of Contributions and Expenditures
finance.notes: As printed in TRACER's Financial Summary (data current as of August 4, 2026; election cycle 2026 County Candidate 4 Year, 12/9/2022-12/3/2026): beginning balance ($3,664.81), total contributions $6,028.00, total expenditures $2,221.45, ending balance $7,312.40. TRACER notes 'Balances for this election cycle have been manually adjusted', and the printed figures do not sum to the ending balance; whether the contribution/expenditure totals are for the report period or cycle-to-date is not stated. The October 13, 2026 report (period 07/31-10/08) was not yet due/posted at retrieval.

people.name: Randall Doizaki
people.bio: Randall Doizaki is the Republican nominee for Jefferson County Sheriff. His campaign says he is a Marine Corps veteran and a retired lieutenant with more than 23 years at the Arapahoe County Sheriff's Office, and that he is currently a lieutenant in Denver Public Schools' Department of Climate and Safety.

people.name: Robert Hennessy
people.bio: Robert Hennessy, a Republican, is the Jefferson County Surveyor and is unopposed on the ballot. BallotReady lists him as surveyor since 2020 and as a professional land surveyor with Rick Engineering Company.

people.name: Nick Lobello
people.bio: Nick Lobello is the Democratic nominee for Jefferson County Coroner. He is a former chief deputy coroner (eight years, per his campaign) and a board-certified medicolegal death investigator; his campaign also lists past work as a firefighter/paramedic and a licensed practical nurse.

people.name: Allison Harmon
people.bio: Allison Harmon is the Republican nominee for Jefferson County Coroner and has cited her experience as a nurse. She announced on June 1 that she was withdrawing because she does not hold the certification a 2024 state law (HB 24-1100) requires of coroners in larger counties, but she did not file to remove her name and remains on the ballot; the county Republican chair says the party wants her to stay in to challenge the law in court.

open_questions: Sheriff: Weston Imer won the June 30 Republican primary (src-critical-report-primaries), but Randall Doizaki is the Republican on the county's general-election candidate list (src-jeffco-on-the-ballot). No source found explaining the switch (withdrawal + vacancy committee is the usual Colorado mechanism, but not confirmed). Imer's campaign site still calls him the 'Republican Nominee' (src-imer-site) and GoodParty.org still lists him (src-goodparty-imer). Doizaki told a Sept. 14 GOP event 'I'm running because I was asked to' (src-ctr-marx-event). Confirm with the Clerk's Elections Division (303-271-8111).

Treasurer: Bob (Robert) Szulczewski was the Republican primary nominee (src-critical-report-primaries); GoodParty.org still lists him as a Republican candidate (src-goodparty-szulczewski), but no Republican is on the county list (src-jeffco-on-the-ballot). No source found on a withdrawal or why no vacancy replacement appears. Hendrickson's Libertarian Party profile says no Republican is running (src-lp-hendrickson). The Jefferson County Republican Party lists Libertarian Murl Hendrickson as its Treasurer candidate on its 'Meet Your 2026 Candidates' page without an explicit endorsement label (src-jeffco-gop-candidates); not recorded as an endorsement.

Campaign finance: TRACER candidate search is a form-postback page that could not be queried through the available tools (src-tracer-search); direct downloads to tracer.sos.colorado.gov (bulk data) were blocked by the network proxy. Only Marinelli's candidate-detail page was reachable via a direct link. Finance for the other 13 candidates is missing; the Oct. 13, 2026 reports will also be new.

Questionnaires: no published written Q&A from the approved outlets (Vote411/LWV Jefferson County, CPR, Colorado Sun, Colorado Community Media, Denver Gazette, Denver Post, Ballotpedia) was found for these county races. Ballotpedia and Colorado Community Media pages returned robots-disallowed; Vote411 requires an address lookup; lwvjeffco.org failed to load. LWV Jefferson County held a county-candidate forum on Oct. 1 (per goldenunited.org; not a written questionnaire). Arvadans For Progressive Action (an advocacy group) published survey answers from Cutter, Hensel, Proctor, Kerr, Ketcham and Lobello (src-apa-2026-guide), not used because it is not on the approved outlet list.

Cutter's 'Jeffco Endorsements' page shows endorsers only as images (filenames suggest Neguse, Zenzinger, Kerr, Bridges, Kolker, Titone, Duran, Stewart, Proctor, others) (src-cutter-jeffco-endorsements); not recorded. Her site's 'Organizations' page appears to be a legacy Senate list and was not used.
Kerr's campaign site shows three unlabeled logos (filenames suggest IBEW, CWF, DALF) (src-kerr-home); only DALF is recorded, from DALF's own page.

Endorsement lists for Kerr, Hensel and Lobello were read through a page-summarizing fetch; spellings should be spot-checked (e.g., Hensel's page reportedly prints 'Brittney Pettersen' and 'Claire Carmelia'; Lobello's page reportedly prints 'Westminister Mayor' with 'Claire Camelia', omitted here pending verification).

Eric Proctor's campaign site (ericproctor.com) blocks automated fetching; website taken from the Jeffco Democrats candidate page. His bio relies partly on his own answers published by Arvadans For Progressive Action.

Paul Poston's site (paulforclerk.com) returned no readable content; no bio beyond nominee status. Vera King has no campaign website found; her bio relies on The Critical Report's one-word description.
Robert Hennessy: incumbency and employer come from BallotReady, not a county biography; the county Leadership page confirms he is the current Surveyor.
Allison Harmon: what happens if she wins without the required certification is unresolved (src-cbs-harmon). No campaign website found.

No sheriff endorsements found from FOP, Jeffco deputies associations or other law-enforcement groups for either Marinelli or Doizaki; Marinelli's campaign site lists no endorsements and Doizaki's site has only individual testimonials. No newspaper editorial endorsements found for any of these county races as of Oct. 9.
